abstract: Dissecting the genetic basis of complex traits and pyramiding favorable alleles are central to crop breeding. However, jointly evaluating pleiotropy and epistasis to identify allele combinations that meet multiple breeding objectives remains challenging. Here, we present BPEA (Bayesian Pleiotropy and Epistasis Analysis), a Bayesian framework integrating LD-guided QTL interval identification, joint genetic inference and allele-combination assessment. BPEA uses the joint posterior to estimate the posterior probability of simultaneous improvement (PPSI) between allele combinations and ranks them by mean PPSI. In simulations, BPEA improved interval identification and epistatic interaction attribution relative to comparator methods and maintained high precision in shared-signal detection. When epistasis was present, it reduced mean combination-selection regret by 68.4-86.3% relative to a model without interaction terms. Applications to three rapeseed populations identified shared genetic signals and candidate epistatic interactions associated with seed-quality traits. BPEA also prioritized allele combinations for simultaneous reductions in erucic acid and glucosinolate contents and identified complementary parents for cross design. BPEA thus provides a framework for genetic dissection and genomics-guided crop improvement.
